examples.ko: 인터넷이 안 돼서 모뎀을 껐다 켰어요.
examples.en: The internet was down, so I turned the modem off and on.
A modem and a router are different devices.

examples.ko: 이 모뎀은 십 년 전에 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought this modem ten years ago.
The lights on the modem do not turn on.

examples.ko: 통신사 기사님이 와서 모뎀을 바꿔 주셨어요.
examples.en: A technician from the carrier came and replaced the modem.
In the old days, modems made a loud noise.

explain: 인터넷이 안 될 때 '모뎀을 껐다 켜 보세요'라는 말을 많이 들어요. 와이파이를 퍼뜨리는 '공유기'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 모뎀은 인터넷 회선과 연결하는 기계예요. 요즘은 둘이 한 기계로 합쳐진 것도 있어요.
explain_en: When the internet fails, you often hear '모뎀을 껐다 켜 보세요'. People mix it up with a '공유기' (router that spreads Wi-Fi), but the modem connects to the internet line. Some devices now combine both.

examples.en: Birds built a nest up in the tree.
My spouse and I set up a small, cozy home.
I made a warm nest for the cat.
We found our newlywed home in Seoul.

examples.ko: 이 집은 우리 가족의 소중한 보금자리예요.
examples.en: This house is our family's precious home.
The abandoned dogs found a new home.

explain: '집'보다 따뜻하고 포근한 느낌이 있어서 글이나 광고에서 자주 보여요. 새나 동물의 둥지에도 쓰고, '신혼 보금자리', '새 보금자리'처럼 새로 시작하는 곳에 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels warmer and cozier than '집', so you often see it in writing and ads. It also works for the nests of birds and animals, and is common in phrases for a fresh start such as '신혼 보금자리' and '새 보금자리'.

examples.en: There were many mosquitoes, so I sprayed insecticide.

examples.ko: 살충제는 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 두세요.
examples.en: Keep insecticide out of children's reach.

examples.ko: 벌레 때문에 살충제 대신 식초물을 써 봤어요.
examples.en: Because of the bugs, I tried vinegar water instead of insecticide.
The smell of the insecticide gave me a headache.
Does this insecticide work well on cockroaches too?
Some flowers are weak against chemical insecticide.

explain: 일상에서는 '모기약', '바퀴벌레약'처럼 벌레 이름을 붙여 부르고, 살충제는 설명서나 뉴스, 농사 이야기에서 더 자주 써요. 식물의 병을 막는 약은 '살균제', 잡초를 없애는 약은 '제초제'라서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life people name the bug, as in 모기약 or 바퀴벌레약, while 살충제 appears more in instructions, news, and farming talk. Medicine that prevents plant disease is 살균제, and that which kills weeds is 제초제, so they differ.

examples.en: A loud noise is coming from the air conditioner's outdoor unit.
The outdoor unit is installed outside the balcony.
In summer, the area around the outdoor unit gets very hot.

examples.ko: 실외기 위에 물건을 올려 두지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't put things on top of the outdoor unit.

examples.ko: 실외기가 고장 나서 시원한 바람이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The outdoor unit is broken, so no cool air comes out.
When I moved, I took the outdoor unit to the new house.

explain: 방 안에 있는 '실내기'와 짝을 이루는 말이에요. 에어컨 이야기에서 가장 많이 나와요. 소리가 나거나 고장 나면 '실외기 때문에 그래요'처럼 원인을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It pairs with '실내기', the indoor unit. It comes up mostly in talk about air conditioners. When there is noise or a breakdown, people name it as the cause, as in '실외기 때문에 그래요'.

en: to be stained; to be smeared

examples.en: Coffee splashed on my white clothes and stained them.

examples.ko: 눈물로 얼룩진 얼굴을 보고 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: It hurt to see her tear-stained face.
The wall is stained because of moisture.
Eat carefully so you don't stain it.

examples.ko: 이 천은 물에 닿으면 쉽게 얼룩져요.
examples.en: This fabric stains easily when it touches water.

examples.ko: 싸움으로 얼룩졌던 지난 한 해를 잊고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to forget last year, which was marred by fights.

explain: '더러워지다'보다 자국이 남는다는 느낌이 강해요. '눈물로 얼룩지다', '슬픔으로 얼룩진 하루'처럼 좋지 않은 일이 가득 찬 시간을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It carries a stronger sense than '더러워지다' (get dirty) that a mark is left behind. It is also used figuratively for a time filled with bad things, as in '눈물로 얼룩지다' (be stained with tears) and '슬픔으로 얼룩진 하루' (a day marred by sadness).

examples.ko: 컵이 우그러져 있어서 새 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: The cup was dented, so I bought a new one.
The pot got dented and is inconvenient to use.
The car door got hit and ended up dented.
When I stepped on the can, it got crushed easily.
I tried straightening the crumpled hat with my hands.
Carry the box carefully so it doesn't get dented.

explain: 눌리거나 부딪혀서 한쪽이 안으로 들어가고 모양이 망가질 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '찌그러지다'를 쓰는 사람도 많아요. 캔, 냄비, 자동차처럼 단단한 물건에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when something is pressed or hit so one side caves in and the shape is spoiled. Many people also say the similar '찌그러지다'. It suits hard objects such as cans, pots and cars.

en: to be cut; to be amputated

examples.en: The power line was cut because of the storm.
I heard one finger was severed in the accident.

examples.ko: 강을 건너는 다리가 절단되면서 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: The bridge over the river was cut and the road was blocked.
A loud sound came from the rope being cut.
The severed cable has to be replaced with a new one.

examples.ko: 이 철사는 힘을 주면 쉽게 절단돼요.
examples.en: This wire cuts easily if you apply force.

explain: 절단되다는 사고나 고장으로 선·줄·길이 끊기거나 몸의 일부가 잘려 나갔을 때 써요. 일부러 자르는 건 '절단하다', 일어난 결과를 말할 땐 '절단되다'예요. 일상에서는 '끊어지다', '잘리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 절단되다 describes the result when a line, rope, road or body part gets severed by an accident or failure; doing it on purpose is 절단하다. In daily speech '끊어지다' or '잘리다' is more natural.

en: to be damaged; to be broken

examples.en: The parcel box was damaged, so I asked for an exchange.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 차량 여러 대가 파손됐어요.
examples.en: Several vehicles were damaged by the typhoon.
Glass products break easily, so be careful.
We replace damaged items for free.

examples.ko: 운반 중에 가구가 파손되지 않게 포장했어요.
examples.en: I packed the furniture so it wouldn't be damaged in transit.
The wall was damaged, so I called a repairman.

explain: 일상에서는 '부서지다'나 '깨지다'를 쓰고, '파손되다'는 배송, 보험, 사고처럼 공식적인 상황에서 많이 써요. '파손 주의', '파손 보상'처럼 명사로도 자주 보여요. 작은 흠집보다는 어느 정도 부서진 상태에 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '부서지다' or '깨지다', while '파손되다' is common in official situations like delivery, insurance and accidents. It also appears as a noun in phrases such as '파손 주의' and '파손 보상'. It suggests something actually broken rather than a small scratch.

p.n: 파손되다 means broken or smashed; 손상되다 may mean only partly harmed.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 마당 옆에 큰 헛간이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a big shed next to the yard at my grandfather's house.
I put the farm tools in the shed.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 헛간 안에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: It rained, so we rested inside the barn for a while.

examples.ko: 헛간 문이 낡아서 잘 안 닫혀요.
examples.en: The shed door is old, so it doesn't close well.

examples.ko: 시골에서는 헛간에 장작이나 연장을 많이 보관해요.
examples.en: In the countryside, people often keep firewood or tools in the shed.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 헛간에서 고양이 새끼를 발견했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I found a kitten in the barn.

explain: '창고'는 물건을 쌓아 두는 건물 전체를 넓게 말하고, '헛간'은 주로 시골집에서 농기구나 장작을 두는 허름한 건물에 써요. 도시에서는 거의 '창고'라고 해요.
explain_en: '창고' is a general word for any building used to store things, while '헛간' mostly means a simple shed on a farm or country house for tools and firewood. In the city people almost always say '창고'.
